cases.customer_question: What exactly are Support Layers and ICS details in Bluetooth qualification, and where can they be viewed?
question_variants: What is included in ICS details?
Are profiles and features the same as ICS?
Where can I view ICS details for a QDID?
What defines the qualified Bluetooth functionality?
What does the Bluetooth SIG register internally?
How detailed is the ICS definition?
cases.actual_issue: Misunderstanding between high-level Bluetooth profiles/features and the detailed ICS definitions actually used in Bluetooth qualification.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The customer assumed that Bluetooth qualification only tracks visible features and profiles. The consultant clarified that the qualification database contains much more detailed ICS definitions describing implemented Bluetooth functionality. These ICS definitions determine whether a modified product is still considered the same qualified design.
cases.consultant_answer: Support Layers and ICS definitions are more detailed than the feature and profile summaries typically visible in a QDID overview. Detailed ICS information is publicly viewable to logged-in SIG members through the 'View ICS Details' interface in the qualification database. The registered ICS definitions determine the qualified Bluetooth implementation and whether a future design change still qualifies as the same design.
cases.decision_logic: Bluetooth qualification reuse depends on detailed ICS-defined functionality, not only high-level profile names. Therefore, evaluating whether a design changed requires reviewing the underlying ICS details.
cases.final_recommendation: Review the detailed ICS definitions associated with the qualified design before determining whether a modification can reuse the existing qualification.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Relying only on visible profile summaries instead of detailed ICS definitions can lead to incorrect assumptions about qualification reuse eligibility and required testing.
